To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ecrg4 expression in the choroid plexer is down-regulated after traumatic brain injury, and augurins immunoreactivity is decreased in the choroid epithelia.
Ecrg4 gene down-regulation and augurin release are part of the initial response to injury while Ecrg4 gene up-regulation is part of the later response.
augurin, an Ecrg4 gene product, is released from the CP in response to brain injury and augurin may play an important inhibitory role in the brain’s response to injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel role for Ecrg4 in the CP as an injury response gene.
the role of Ecrg4 in TBI and the potential of augurin as a therapeutic agent in CNS injury.
a novel role for Ecrg4 in the regulation of the composition of CSF and its potential role in the regulation of CNS repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
augurin is a choroid plexed derived injury response gene.
Ecrg4 is an injury response gene that regulates the composition of CSF by modulating augurin production in the CP.
Ecrg4 gene down-regulation is a novel injury response that may be dysinhibitory for brain regeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
augurin is released from CPe in response to injury and that augurin may be a novel injury response gene that regulates neuroprogenitor growth and differentiation.

the choroid plesus, by virtue of its ability regulate CSF composition, is an important regulator of brain homeostasis that responds to CNS injury by down-regulating augurin, a hormone-like peptide that regulates senescence and neuroprogenitor growth and differentiation in normal brain.
Ecrg4 is a CP-derived injury response gene and augurin is a hormone-like protein that is released in response to CNS injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choroid plevus is the site of injury-induced gene expression and augerine release that can be used for therapeutic purposes.
Ecrg4 is a CP-derived injury response gene that is rapidly down-regulated by TBI.
the CP is a dynamic structure that responds to injury by producing growth regulatory factors.
